question.text: Kaveri Credit Opportunities Fund (Cat II AIF) is crediting FY25 income to Mr. Arjun Menon (resident individual) — his share: INR 40 lakh interest, INR 15 lakh LTCG on unlisted debt, INR 5 lakh dividend. Under Section 194LBB, what TDS must the fund withhold before crediting?

answer.text: TDS at 10% on the entire INR 60 lakh = INR 6,00,000
TDS at 30% on interest and 12.5% on LTCG and 10% on dividend = INR 14,37,500
No TDS — pass-through means tax is the LP's responsibility
TDS at 20% on all three heads = INR 12,00,000

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 194LBB mandates the Investment Fund to deduct tax at 10% on income (other than business income) distributed or credited to a RESIDENT investor, irrespective of the head of income. 10% of INR 60 lakh = INR 6 lakh. The LP Mr. Menon then claims this TDS as credit in his ITR and pays balance tax at his slab/head-wise rates. The Trap: Option B confuses head-wise final tax rates with the 194LBB withholding rate. Option C ignores the explicit 194LBB obligation on the fund. Option D applies the non-resident dividend WHT rate of 20% — that's 194LBB(b), not (a). Cross-Exam Context: XXIV (AML) and III-A/C (Compliance) cover the CA verification of Form 64C/64D. XIX-C asks the manager to run the TDS deduction engine correctly. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cut TDS challans under the fund's TAN in the month of credit — not the month of actual distribution. Section 115UB deems year-end un-distributed income as credited; miss this and you attract Section 201 interest and disallowance.
